text:
Samira K.: quick question 1pm demo ruined by vacuum symphony. I made a tiny "printer-box booth" around my mic (cardboard + blanket) and it actually helps. anyone tried DIY mic hammocks or other weird hacks? :thinking:
Jon: love the ingenuity. mic hammock = rubber bands + desk arm + sock. keeps desk rumble away. cardboard booth is top-tier for mid-high freq.
Maya: if you go cardboard, line it with a towel or bath mat to absorb more. also angle it so the mic faces away from the open door.
Samira K.: good call. also my upload dipped during the demo: ```
Ping: 36 ms
DL: 14.1 Mbps
UL: 0.8 Mbps
```
Ethan: upload under 1 Mbps is brutal for video calls. options: tether phone (5G if available), borrow a travel router, or plug laptop into ethernet if you can run a cable.
Jon: double-NAT with a travel router in front of ISP modem works; run travel router as AP and enable QoS to prioritize your laptop. small Ubiquiti AP makes this painless.
Maya: also check for cloud backups or software updates running in background 1 those love to eat upload.
NetBot: Provider advisory: maintenance earlier in your area (Ticket #MAINT-2026-992). Estimated restore: 1950009800. Visit provider status page for details.
Samira K.: of course maintenance. thanks for the hammock idea; testing now. will post a pic of the box booth + sock-hammock if it survives the next vacuum solo.
Ethan: obligatory: photo or it didn't happen. bonus points for a dramatic vacuum-face. :camera_with_flash:
Jon: if you need a spare AP, I have one you can borrow this week 1 DM me.
Maya: pro tip: mute while vacuum is loud and use chat to apologize. surprisingly effective.
Samira K.: ha will do. thanks team 1 deploying cardboard bunker now, updates incoming.
